ideaStatement: Add an optional, user-initiated Jev (TypeSafe) typed-decision layer to the CSM skills: off by default, enabled by a global switch via a request/2 decision field, a --use-jev flag, or a natural-language phrase; non-safety decision points may apply (guarded routing, add-only review, reversible internals) while every acceptance, security, and completion gate stays deterministic; all other points are recorded advice; the host-mediated transport fails open to the skill's existing harness model when Jev is unreachable or out of credit.

researchSynthesis: The layer is grounded in a three-stage research program: Jev deep research, an ability-to-skill mapping, and a change design, then an independent adversarial challenge, a live 20-call experiment, a 195-item 227-call calibration, and an independent verification. Live-verified: POST https://openrouter.ai/api/alpha/decisions with OPENROUTER_ROUTER_KEY returns typed decisions for typesafe/jev-1.13 (~$0.0000211/call, median 329ms, output free); the choice space is the criteria record's keys (criteria is required); the native api.typesafe.ai endpoint rejects this key; the chat endpoint rejects the model. The skills currently use subagent LLM fan-out for generation and deterministic code for most typed decisions; csm-orchestrate has no model runtime and an explicitly injected executor, so the adapter is injected the same way. Calibration reached 94.9% on a synthetic rule-labelled corpus but found no validated auto-accept gate: five of six derived thresholds are 'accept everything', the one structured point still auto-accepts its confident errors (privacy->security 0.94, data-integrity->destructive 0.86), confidence is not the argmax probability in 106/195 cases, and no human-labelled held-out set exists; injection was resisted 0/8 and repeats were byte-stable. The SCOUT corrected four finding errors: csm-plan already declares broker/host-mediated egress (only csm-build and csm-review are disabled/none); routing spans two seams (run-orchestrator.mjs:437 and phase-compiler.mjs:169-206); the adapter must live under csm-orchestrate/lib/** because root lib/ is not packed; and capabilities/3 plus request/2 are unavoidable because the schemas are additionalProperties:false. The DEEP_DIVE confirmed the design is integrable without touching any gate, provided three constraints hold: the adapter stays in the packed skill tree, decision data never enters the per-node request or receipt (materialDigest strips only status/requestDigest), and opt-in uses a real request/2 rather than an added field. The dominant residual risk is call-count and latency blow-up inside retry/remediation/review loops, boundable with per-point call caps, single-flight and in-run result caching, a run-scoped circuit breaker, and a kill switch; the dominant correctness risk is applying a confidently-wrong adjacent-taxonomy classification, mitigated by restricting applies to reversible non-authoritative points, add-only review, deterministic-baseline agreement, and an audit artifact per applied decision. Fail-open behavior is specified: out-of-credit (402), uncontactable (network/timeout/5xx), rate-limited (429), auth/permission (401/403), and model/config errors all revert to the harness model or deterministic baseline, record a skipped decision, and never pause the skill; Jev quota is distinct from the main-model Pause On Quota. Re-validation (2026-09-19) against main f2a654d after the in-loop completion enforcement landed (e07d84a): the architecture stays valid but is not execution-ready. Full delta, per-decision/per-phase verdicts, and 11 prioritized adaptations are in the linked finding .agents/research/2026-09-19-jev-optin-revalidation-20260919t150000z-jevoptinreval-research.json (sha256:6c94ee9cdc24ebd330919a8b9a475519e9941457c3ab7d350be7c5515ed987e7). Blocking adaptations: re-anchor requestDigest csm-orchestrate/lib/index.mjs :806 -> :872; register csm-orchestrate-request/2 and csm-orchestrate-capabilities/3 in schemas/registry.json and schemas/compatibility-matrix.json; make csm-orchestrate/lib/capabilities.mjs revision-aware while preserving .skills[].activation.mode; dual-accept request/2 in csm-orchestrate/lib/intake.mjs; pack csm-orchestrate/decision-points.json; add the .agents/decisions/ index class; and extend the never-Jev boundary to evaluator contracts, loop guards, binding receipts, closure/verification status, and the supersession cursor. Re-validation v2 (2026-09-19) against HEAD 9314599 (which includes the in-loop completion enforcement e07d84a plus the off-surface daemon/corpus fixes): the architecture is unchanged and still valid, but the earlier re-validation under-specified the integration. Two defect-class corrections: (a) csm-orchestrate/lib/index.mjs now assigns requestDigest at BOTH :872 and :1225, so byte-identity work covers two sites; (b) intake.mjs performs no runtime JSON-schema validation, so request/2 opt-in requires a new registered schema AND marker/field extension, not a validator change. One scope correction: the never-Jev boundary must enumerate the full enforcement surface — schema-registry immutability, csm-verification-status/1, build completion.commit/rollback status, artifact lifecycleStatus+descriptorDigest, digest anti-fabrication, the security/isolation gate set, classifyResume/retryDecision, and review terminal immutability — and Jev output must be csm-orchestrate-decision-gate/1-class (observational, no acceptance authority); seven enforcement receipt ids remain unregistered and must be code-constructed only. Also confirmed: decision-points.json needs an explicit pack mapping; the .agents/decisions/ index class needs an agents-index entry and a "## decisions/" heading; the <500 SKILL cap leaves ~23/27 lines in csm-build/csm-deep-research. Full evidence and independent challenge/judge outcomes are in the linked v2 finding (sha256:2e5d9a3a82f71c9cdb80ac7fec8c20b776728d3783f121b8e079e83a6e5ba1fd).
